title: Italian cinema, from neorealism to Fellini

questions.question: In Vittorio De Sica's film of 1948, a poor man in Rome finds work at last, but on his first day something he needs for the job is stolen. What?
questions.hint: His job is to put up posters on walls. He and his small son Bruno search the whole of Rome for it.
questions.explanation: The film is Bicycle Thieves, "Ladri di biciclette". The father was played by Lamberto Maggiorani, a factory worker who had never acted. In 1950 Hollywood gave the film a special Oscar as the best foreign film shown in America the year before.

questions.question: In a famous scene of the film La dolce vita (1960), the Swedish actress Anita Ekberg wades at night into a fountain in Rome. Which one?
options: The Fountain of the Four Rivers
questions.hint: It is the largest Baroque fountain in Rome. Visitors throw a coin into it over their shoulder, to be sure of coming back to the city.
questions.explanation: Ekberg calls to Marcello Mastroianni, who follows her into the water. The film also gave the world the word "paparazzi", from the name of one of its characters, the photographer Paparazzo. The fountain itself was finished in 1762.

questions.question: Which Italian actress won the Oscar for best actress for De Sica's film Two Women ("La ciociara")? It was the first Oscar ever given to an actor for a part in a foreign language.
questions.hint: She grew up in Pozzuoli, near Naples. She often played opposite Marcello Mastroianni, as in Marriage Italian Style.
questions.explanation: Sophia Loren won the Oscar in April 1962 for her part as a mother who flees the war with her daughter. The film is based on a novel by Alberto Moravia. Anna Magnani had won the same prize in 1956, but for a film in English, The Rose Tattoo.

questions.question: Which film studios, opened in Rome in 1937, became the home of Italian cinema and the place where Fellini made most of his films?
questions.hint: In the 1950s so many American films were made there, such as Ben-Hur, that people called it "Hollywood on the Tiber".
questions.explanation: Mussolini opened Cinecittà, "Cinema City", on 28 April 1937. From 1944 its buildings housed refugees for some years, which is one reason why the neorealist directors filmed in the streets. Fellini worked for decades in Studio 5, for a long time its largest stage.

questions.question: Who directed Rome, Open City (1945), the film about the Resistance that made Italian neorealism famous around the world?
questions.hint: A few years later the Hollywood star Ingrid Bergman left her husband for him, and it was a great scandal. The actress Isabella is their daughter.
questions.explanation: Rossellini began shooting in January 1945, only months after the Germans had left Rome, when film stock was very hard to find. Anna Magnani's run behind the German lorry is one of the most famous scenes in cinema. The young Federico Fellini, then 24, helped to write the script.

questions.question: Who played Gelsomina, the simple girl sold to a travelling strongman, in Fellini's La strada (1954)?
questions.hint: She was the director's wife, from 1943 until his death fifty years later. She also played the lead in his Nights of Cabiria.
questions.explanation: Giulietta Masina played Gelsomina like a sad clown, and critics compared her to Charlie Chaplin. Zampanò, the strongman, was played by the Mexican-born American actor Anthony Quinn. The music is by Nino Rota, who wrote for every Fellini film from 1952 to 1979.

questions.question: Why did Fellini call his film of 1963 "8½"?
options: It was his age when he first saw a film
It was the length of the film in reels
It was the number of films he had made
It was the number of weeks of filming
questions.hint: The film is about a famous director, played by Marcello Mastroianni, who has no idea what his next film will be. Fellini could not think of a title either.
questions.explanation: Fellini counted six full films, plus two short ones and one made together with another director, each worth a half: seven and a half. The new film was number eight and a half. Many directors have since made films about making films, but this one is the model.

questions.question: In Luchino Visconti's The Leopard (1963), set in Sicily in the 1860s, who plays the ageing Prince of Salina?
questions.hint: He had begun as a circus acrobat. Visconti did not want him at first, but the producers insisted.
questions.explanation: Burt Lancaster was a Hollywood star, and his voice was dubbed into Italian. Alain Delon plays his nephew Tancredi and Claudia Cardinale the beautiful Angelica. The film, from the novel by Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa, won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1963.

questions.question: In 1948 Luchino Visconti made a film with the real fishermen of a Sicilian village, who spoke their own dialect. It is based on Giovanni Verga's novel I Malavoglia. What is it called?
questions.hint: Visconti went to Sicily to make a short documentary with money from the Communist Party, and stayed for months. The dialect was so hard to follow that a voice in Italian was added.
questions.explanation: La terra trema, "The Earth Trembles", was shot at Aci Trezza, near Catania, the village of Verga's novel. Nobody in it was a professional actor. It failed in the cinemas, but it is now seen as one of the great works of neorealism.

questions.question: Four of Fellini's films won the Oscar for best foreign-language film. Which of these did NOT?
questions.hint: It won the Palme d'Or at Cannes, and the Vatican's newspaper attacked it as immoral. At the Oscars it took only the prize for costumes.
questions.explanation: La dolce vita was not even Italy's candidate for the foreign-film Oscar. Fellini's four winners were La strada, Nights of Cabiria, 8½ and Amarcord. In March 1993, seven months before he died, he received an honorary Oscar for his life's work.
